title: Pro-etale locality and pullback of dualizable condensed sheaves
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $D(T,\Lambda)=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_T)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with ordinary derived tensor and unit $\Lambda_T[0]$, and $D_{\mathrm{lis}}(T,\Lambda)$ for its full subcategory of dualizable objects (objects admitting evaluation and coevaluation satisfying both triangle identities). For a profinite set $S$, use the analogous notation for sheaves on profinite sets over $S$, with finite jointly surjective covering families and coefficient ring the restriction of $\Lambda$ to that site. For every morphism of schemes $f:T\to X$, the coefficient identification $f^*\Lambda_X\cong\Lambda_T$ makes inverse image an exact symmetric monoidal functor $f^*:D(X,\Lambda)\to D(T,\Lambda)$. It preserves dualizable objects and commutes with the scalar extensions $\Lambda_X\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P$, where $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$ and $P\in D(R)$ [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor]. Moreover, for every pro-etale covering family $\{U_i\to X\}$ and every $K\in D(X,\Lambda)$,
$$K\text{ is dualizable}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad K|_{U_i}\text{ is dualizable for every }i.$$
There is no quasi-compactness or bound on irreducible components of $X$ or $U_i$ in this assertion.

proof.text: The coefficient isomorphism of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] makes module inverse image F exact, with exact termwise derived functor D(F) [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Use the explicit balanced relative tensor comparisons of [new-integral-residue-ordinary-monoidal] and their braided identity [new-integral-residue-ordinary-braiding]. The functor preserves flat modules by [new-proetale-inverse-image-module-flat], after identifying scalar extension along the coefficient isomorphism with restriction along its inverse. Apply the source library's Functor.leftDerivedFunctorBraided: its tensor comparison is obtained on K-flat resolutions, with the Koszul braiding inherited from complexes. Transport this strong braided structure along F.leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory. Functor.Monoidal.natTransIsMonoidal_of_transport and Functor.LaxBraided.ofNatIso prove that this transport respects the braiding. Exactness gives triangulatedness of D(F).

Apply $Lf^*$ to a dual, its evaluation and coevaluation, inserting its invertible tensor and unit comparisons. Functoriality and monoidal coherence carry both triangle identities to the image. Hence inverse image preserves dualizable objects.

For $P\in D(R)$, [def-zl-condensed-scalar-realization] writes scalar realization on $Y$ as $D(p_Y^*)(N_P)$, where $N_P=D(e^{-1})Lc^*\underline P$ on the point is independent of $Y$; the constant complex is [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor]. Evaluate the natural derived module comparison of [lem-zl-condensed-point-module-comparison] at $N_P$. This gives $Lf^*(\Lambda_X\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P)\cong\Lambda_T\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P$, naturally in $P$.

For K choose a functorial K-flat resolution P and the source-library DerivedCategory.DualizabilityDatum for P. Its morphism χ models [P,1] tensor P → [P,P]; DualizabilityDatum.isDualizable_Q_obj_iff says K is dualizable exactly when a=Q(χ) is invertible. For a weakly etale f, abelian sheaf pullback is restriction and has an exact left adjoint: left Kan extension over the discrete set of lifts, then sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-localization-kan-discrete-lifts]. Its ordinary closed comparison implies the projection formula. Lift this adjunction to internal modules using [def-sfb-modobj-linearization-transport-adjunction], and compose with the inverse coefficient-transport equivalence. The resulting left adjoint is exact because its underlying abelian functor is exact and coefficient transport is an equivalence. The native module closed comparison is invertible by [lem-proetale-pullback-internal-hom], and inverse image preserves flat modules by [new-proetale-inverse-image-module-flat]. Thus the source-library DualizabilityDatum.isDualizable_Q_obj_map_iff applies: f* K is dualizable exactly when f* a is invertible. This is the proved private helper condensed_dualizability_test; its comparison with the published upperStar is induced by extendScalarsIsoComapInv and exact localization. If every cover restriction of K is dualizable, every restriction of a is invertible, so a is invertible by [lem-zl-condensed-cover-restriction-conservative]. Conversely Step 2 preserves any dual. No finiteness or nonempty-cover assumption occurs.
